newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FORECAST-ANZ year net seen up 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FORECAST-ANZ year net seen up 10 pct.

text.p: Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd (ANZ) is expected to announce its second annual profit of over A$1 billion on Wednesday but profit growth will not be as strong as in previous years, analysts said.
Analysts forecast ANZ's profit before abnormals and after preference share dividends at an average of A$1.05 billion for the year to September 30, 1996.
A result in line with expections would give ANZ annual profit growth of 10.2 percent, below the 28.6 percent growth it reported last year.
Forecasts ranged from A$1.02 billion to A$1.03 billion.

While the bank would benefit from lower tax expenses in the second half and some rise in non-interest revenues, expenses were seen up on last year due to higher staff numbers, wage increases and other branch overheads, analysts said.

"In general overheads, there's...the cost of their new telephone centre in which there is a degree of duplication costs, while they're trying to migrate customers out of the branches and into electronic forms of processing," said Macquarie Equities analyst Graham Maloney.
In early May, ANZ employees won pay rises averaging 14 percent over two years.
At the time, the bank said it did not expect the pay rises to significantly hit profits.

Analysts said growing competition in the home lending market would have narrowed the bank's margins in fiscal 1995/96 but the greatest impact of ANZ's decision in June to enter the home lending price war in would emerge in the current financial year.
"Spreads will be down somewhere between 10 and 15 basis points in the second half (of 1995/96) but the major thing is the big impact won't hit them until 1997," one analyst said.
Analysts saw ANZ's bad and doubtful debts charge rising to an average A$213 million from A$174 million a year ago but many noted the figure would be near historical lows for the bank.
Some analysts said overshadowing the result would be any comments from ANZ on future staff cuts, which is seen as a major avenue for cost reductions in the bank.
"The major issue for ANZ moving forward is this issue of costs. (The market is looking for) some comment on labour shedding," an analyst said.

ANZ is involved in an ongoing dispute with its Finance Sector Union employees, which have been holding stop work meetings around the country in recent weeks to consider wider industrial action over feared staff reductions.
ANZ reported a net profit after abnormals of A$1.05 billion in the year to September 30, 1995 from A$822 million in 1993/94.
